key_image.thumbnail_test: At reduced size, the two weighted impulses, their two shifted responses, and the final four-sample sum must remain distinguishable; secondary derivation labels may recede but the input-to-output assembly must not.

contiguous_three_tap_hand_case.note: This is the corrected three-tap hand example and supplies figures 1 and 2. Do not replace it with the brief's older two-tap h=[1,-1] case.

finite_buffer_two_tap_case.note: This intentionally remains a two-tap implementation example and supplies figure 3.

sparse_physical_echo_case.note: This is a sparse three-nonzero-tap physical echo, not the contiguous hand kernel and not the demo's compact adjacent coefficient display. It supplies figure 4.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: The prose gives the four sums, but only a step sequence makes the reversal-and-shift bookkeeping and changing overlap perceptible. It is the lesson's procedural first exposure and is not duplicated by the later representation comparison.
figures.tier_reason: The graphic is a four-state geometric process on one small integer grid with short labels. A sourced diagram would add foreign notation, and a static component cannot provide the required one-change-per-frame sequence API.

figures.teaching_claim: Flip, shift, multiply, and sum are four views of the same index rule h[n-m], with zero extension controlling the edge frames.

fixed_elements: top x[m] row with cells m=-2 through 4 and x[0]=1, x[1]=2

product row and one output badge y[n]

zero-extension cells shown as dashed muted ghosts
shared_layout.frame_delta: Only n, the horizontal placement of h[n-m], the active overlap cells, product values, and the y[n] badge change. All axes, rows, dimensions, and label positions remain pixel-identical.

color_roles.green_#5aa46a: active products and completed output sum

acceptance: All four output values equal [1,2.5,1.25,0.5].
The kernel is visibly flipped as a function of m before it shifts.
No connected line implies interpolation between discrete cells.
Zero-extension ghosts remain visible in every frame.
Frame dimensions and fixed geometry are identical.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: This is the conceptual bridge from one measured response to every LTI response. The surrounding derivation is symbolic; the figure binds the two separate LTI clauses to the concrete corrected three-tap result and carries the lesson's key-image burden.
figures.tier_reason: The configured key image requires figures/impulse-decomposition.svg. The composition can remain a simple two-branch diagram with short formula labels; avoid paragraph text or TeX constructs that would force a component.
figures.source_status: house drawing; no sourced image because this is an explanation rather than an artefact
figures.embed: <Figure src="./figures/impulse-decomposition.svg" alt="The input x=[1,2] splits into a unit impulse and a twice-weighted delayed impulse; one LTI response becomes h[n] and 2h[n-1], which add to [1,2.5,1.25,0.5]." caption="Linearity preserves the weights and sum; time invariance reuses one impulse response at each shift." />
figures.teaching_claim: The convolution result follows by reusing one h[n]: linearity preserves weights and addition, while time invariance preserves shifts.
figures.composition: Read left-to-right and then top-to-bottom: one input splits into two vertically aligned branches, each passes through an identical T block, and the two response ledgers merge into one output ledger. Use alignment rather than a separate hue for each term.

color_roles.currentColor: T blocks, operators, indices, and explanatory labels

acceptance: The branch ledgers add samplewise to [1,2.5,1.25,0.5].
The figure explicitly names which equality uses linearity and which uses time invariance.
m is used only as a local decomposition/convolution dummy if the generic sum is shown; n remains the output index.
The central assembly remains intelligible at key-image thumbnail scale.
The SVG contains no fixed width or height and uses currentColor for theme-dependent text and strokes.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: This figure makes the finite-buffer contract operational: the algebraic sum, batch matrix, and streaming state machine agree only with the same coefficient order, zero initialization, emitted indices, and tail flush. Neither the flip sequence nor the demo teaches that implementation equivalence.
figures.tier_reason: Three coordinated panels contain a matrix, formulas, explanatory labels, and cross-panel bindings. House typography requires HTML layout and KaTeX rather than hand-positioned SVG text.
figures.source_status: house component inspired by Orfanidis Chapter 4 §§4.1 and 4.3; no sourced diagram
figures.embed: <Figure name="ConvolutionThreeViews" alt="Three aligned panels compute x=[1,2,-1] convolved with h=[1,0.5] as overlap sums, a four-by-three Toeplitz matrix product, and a one-sample streaming buffer with a final zero flush." caption="The sum, matrix, and state buffer agree only when coefficient order, zero initialization, output range, and final flush agree." />
figures.teaching_claim: Batch and streaming convolution are the same dependency graph under one explicit finite-boundary contract.

color_roles.green_palette: emitted output and successful equality across views
color_roles.ink_and_muted_palette: matrix structure, inactive state, and support labels

acceptance: All math is rendered with the shared M/KaTeX component, never raw formula strings.
Corresponding current and previous contributions carry the same role colors in all three panels.

The component is hook-free, uses inline styles and palette.ts, contains no Tailwind, and remains readable at the standard figure width.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: This is the physical interpretation and demo bridge: it turns three nonzero coefficients into dry, early, and late paths with sample and millisecond units. The other figures use adjacent taps and cannot communicate audible delay scale.
figures.tier_reason: A simple three-branch signal-flow diagram and aligned transient timeline need only short labels and arrows. It is explanatory, so a sourced audio schematic would be inferior and unnecessary.
figures.source_status: house drawing; no sourced image or credit entry
figures.embed: <Figure src="./figures/sparse-echo-paths.svg" alt="At 8 kilohertz, one input splits into a dry path at zero delay, an early echo with gain a at 400 samples or 50 milliseconds, and a late echo with gain b at 960 samples or 120 milliseconds, then recombines without wraparound." caption="A sparse echo kernel creates dry, 50 ms, and 120 ms copies on one ordinary linear time axis." />
figures.teaching_claim: A sparse three-tap FIR is three shifted copies on the integer line; sample rate converts their index delays to physical time without introducing circular wrap.

paths: early: gain a, delay 400 samples = 50 ms
late: gain b, delay 960 samples = 120 ms

required_labels: a and b are dimensionless gains
figures.composition: Top: input fans into three left-to-right paths and rejoins at one sum node. Bottom: one input transient and its three output copies share an axis marked at 0, 400, and 960 samples, with the millisecond values directly below the same ticks.

color_roles.currentColor: sum node, axes, units, and output

acceptance: 400/8000=50 ms and 960/8000=120 ms are printed next to their matching sample delays.
The axis is visibly linear and contains no return arrow or modulo-N notation.
The sparse delays are not drawn as adjacent n=0,1,2 taps.
The figure does not substitute the demo truth vector [0.70,0.25,0.10] for the generic physical gains 1,a,b.
Every color role is also named and separated by path position for monochrome accessibility.

global_visual_rules.reading_order: left-to-right for signal flow; top-to-bottom for decomposition and aligned representations
global_visual_rules.palette: currentColor plus amber #e2903a, blue #4c8dd6, and green #5aa46a only
global_visual_rules.theme_contract: Raw SVG text and strokes use currentColor; secondary labels use opacity rather than fixed gray. Components use palette.ts and site ink/muted values. No white baked backgrounds.
global_visual_rules.accessibility: Color is redundant with position, path names, cell borders, and text labels. Alt text is factual and one sentence; captions state the takeaway and do not repeat every label.
global_visual_rules.math_notation: Use n as output/sample index and m as the local convolution dummy. Preserve decimal points and minus signs exactly. Do not use k as the convolution dummy.
global_visual_rules.sourcing: All four visuals explain course-owned abstractions or calculations; none is an authenticity-bearing artefact, photograph, scan, or measured plot. Sourced count is therefore zero.

raw_svg: Render each of the six SVG files individually with npm run figure -- <path> and inspect the PNG.
Render each final SVG with --dark and inspect again; do not infer dark-theme success from source code.
For the four sequence frames, compare dimensions and fixed-pixel geometry and verify one pedagogical delta per frame.
component: Render ConvolutionThreeViews by path before registry landing and by registered name afterward, in light and dark themes.
Run npx tsc --noEmit and npx eslint components/figures after component and registry changes.
Reject red source text, broken KaTeX, clipped matrix brackets, crossed connector lines, or panel labels that become illegible at standard width.
page: After all four comments are landed, run npm run preview -- digital-signal-processing impulse-response-and-convolution.
Inspect both full-page and figures-only light/dark screenshots for caption wrap, scale consistency, sequence controls, and key-image legibility.
Run npm run validate -- digital-signal-processing and require zero missing-figure errors; in particular, the configured key image must exist.
visual_rejection_conditions: any clipped label, axis, matrix bracket, path, or caption
any output value other than the reconciled arrays
a connected curve that implies between-sample interpolation
a sparse echo drawn with circular wrap
fixed black text or strokes that disappear in dark theme
the flip-and-slide frames changing layout in addition to overlap
a key image that is unreadable at thumbnail scale
